bindings.name: SettingsKeyStatus
bindings.go: app_settings.go (App.SettingsKeyStatus); consumed by frontend/src/utils/crypto.js refreshStatus()
bindings.notes: FIRST bridge call of the whole app: settingsStore.js runs decryptSettings() at module-import time whenever localStorage has a `settings` key. If it throws, credentialState becomes 'nostore' and the Settings modal shows a warning banner (invisible on the Operations tab, but wrong). If NO sensitive field in the seeded settings starts with `enc:`, SettingsOpen is never called — so seed plaintext credentials and this is the only settings binding that runs.

bindings.name: LoadHistory

bindings.notes: This is what fills the 'Recent history' strip at the bottom of the Operations panel (RecentHistory.svelte shows $historyStore.slice(0,5)). History is NO LONGER localStorage — it comes from SQLite through this binding. Fields RecentHistory reads: timestamp, operation, success, oid, targets.length, duration, and either results[0].result.value (GET/SET/GETNEXT) or totalResults (WALK/GETBULK). getHistoryDisplayName() resolves entry.oid against the MIB tree, so 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2 renders as 'ifTable'. Timestamps are formatted with toLocaleString('fr-FR') — always dd/mm/yyyy hh:mm:ss regardless of app locale; pick a day > 12 so it does not read as a US date. Mixing one failed entry (red, circle-x icon) in makes the strip look real.

Called with (tableInfo.oid, instances) where instances is the UNION of row instances across every target, in Map insertion order. areas.visual:
HERO = a WALK of ifTable on 10.20.0.1, table view on, index decoded, 12 rows. Concretely: dark theme, MIB tree expanded to ifTable (selected, highlighted) at 400px, operation tab bar with WALK active, OID field pre-filled '1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2', 'Saved queries (6)', then the green result card headed '10.20.0.1' with a '412ms' badge, 'Base OID: 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2 · Results found: 144', the Raw/Table toggle sitting on Table, and a 13-column table whose first column is the DECODED index header 'ifIndex' (not the word 'Index' — that is the un-decoded fallback and it means MibDecodeIndexes failed). Rows read ifIndex 1..12 in numeric order (10 after 9 — that ordering IS the feature), ifType as 'ethernetCsmacd(6)' / 'softwareLoopback(24)' / 'ieee8023adLag(161)', ifAdminStatus/ifOperStatus as 'up(1)' / 'down(2)' / 'dormant(5)', ifSpeed as '1,000,000,000', ifLastChange as '12d 7h 6m 23s (106,238,300)', ifInOctets as '3,874,192,055', ifPhysAddress as '00:1B:21:3C:4D:5E'. Two interfaces are visibly not up — ifIndex 3 (admin up / oper down, ifInErrors 1174) and ifIndex 5 (admin down / oper down) — plus ifIndex 11 dormant(5); that is the mix that makes it read as a real network rather than a demo. Two ifDescr values are long enough to ellipsise inside the 200px cell ('GigabitEthernet0/0/1 - uplink to core-rtr-01 Te0/0/3, 1000BASE-…'), which shows the layout holding up. Footer line: '12 row(s) x 12 column(s) — Click any cell to use its OID in GET/SET'. Below it the Recent-history strip with five entries (WALK/GET/SET/GETBULK plus one red failed GET) — that strip is the difference between 'a screenshot of a tool' and 'a screenshot of someone's Tuesday'. Aim for exactly 12 rows: .table-view-results is max-height 500px, so ~14 rows is the point where an inner scrollbar appears and the shot loses its bottom edge.

SECOND SHOT — raw view, same walk: click 'Raw View', then type 'Errors' or '/oper|admin/' into the filter box; the count chip reads '24 / 144' beside it and each row shows the green MIB name divided from the grey OID. This is the shot that proves the filter and the OID resolution.

THIRD SHOT — device comparison: same WALK but with both targets configured, then click 'Compare'. You get the delta table (OID | Name | 10.20.0.1 | 10.20.0.2 | Delta | % Diff) with rows colour-coded identical/different/missing. Make the two switches genuinely differ — a Juniper sysDescr against a Cisco one, different interface counts so some rows are 'missing', counters an order of magnitude apart so Delta and % Diff are non-trivial. Sort by Delta descending for the shot.

FOURTH SHOT — the careful-app moment: SET tab with sysLocation selected, the SetConfirmModal open showing OID + name, the new value, the type and both target addresses, with the 'don't ask again' checkbox. It is the frame that says this tool writes to production devices and knows it.

Avoid: single-target GET with one field (empty-looking), Anonymous Mode (masks the addresses to 'Device-1'), an empty saved-queries counter, and a table whose first column header says 'Index' in italics — all three read as an unfinished app.
hazards: NOTHING IN localStorage PRODUCES RESULTS. `bulkResults` is component-local state in OperationsPanel.svelte (line 43) and is only ever assigned inside handleSnmpGet/handleSnmpWalk/etc. A scene cannot pre-seed it. The capture bootstrap MUST drive the DOM after mount. The cheapest deterministic sequence for the hero: (1) click the ifTable node in the MIB tree — MibPanel dispatches 'select', and OperationsPanel's reactive block (lines 96-132) then sets activeOperation='WALK' AND snmpWalkOid=node.oid automatically for a Table/Row node, so no typing is needed; (2) click the Execute button, `document.querySelector('.operation-form .btn-primary')`. With autoGetEnabled:true, selecting a Scalar/Column instead fires a GET on its own after a 100ms setTimeout — that is the zero-click path for a GET scene. The filter box and the Compare/Comparison/Table-view toggles are all local state too and need the same treatment (the filter is `bind:value`, so set .value then dispatch a real 'input' event).

A MISSING EXPORT IS A BLANK PAGE, not a missing method: the stub module is imported statically, so one absent name throws 'does not provide an export named X' and the app never mounts. The Operations dependency graph alone needs: SnmpGet, SnmpSet, SnmpSetMultiple, SnmpWalk, SnmpGetNext, SnmpGetBulk, ResolveOids (OperationsPanel.svelte:2) and MibTable, MibDecodeIndexes, MibEncodeIndex (ResultsDisplay.svelte:17). Booting the shell around it additionally needs GetPersistentMibDirectory, ListMibFiles, ImportMibFiles, TraySetLabels, LoadAllMibs, LoadEnabledMibs, LoadMibsWithDiagnostics, SaveHistoryEntry, LoadHistory, DeleteHistoryEntry, DeleteHistoryEntries, ClearHistory, ImportHistoryEntries, SettingsSeal, SettingsOpen, SettingsAdoptKey, SettingsKeyStatus, SettingsForgetKey. Every one must return a Promise — the real bindings all do.

LEADING DOTS ARE THE COMMONEST WAY TO GET A BLANK TABLE. Walk item OIDs carry a leading dot ('.1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.2.2') because they come from gosnmp; MIB tree OIDs and the MibTable column OIDs do not. tableRows.matchColumn strips the dot on the item side only, so a fixture that omits the dot on walk items still matches, but oidInfoCache lookups (`oidInfoCache[item.oid]`) are exact-string — if ResolveOids is keyed without the dot while the walk items have it, every MIB name and every enum decode silently disappears and the table shows bare integers. Keep both sides identical to what SnmpWalk returned.

TABLE VIEW NEEDS THE TREE, NOT JUST THE WALK. canShowTableView() requires a node with mibType 'Table' or 'Row' AND at least one 'Column' child. With no node selected it falls back to autoDetectedTableNode, which walks up .parent references that mibStore adds after LoadMibsWithDiagnostics — so the stub must return {tree, diagnostics} (an object, not a bare array) and must NOT include a `parent` field itself. Also: auto-detection only fires for results whose envelope type is exactly 'WalkResponse'; a GETBULK renders raw unless a Table/Row is selected.

THE TABLE RENDERS EVERY COLUMN THE TREE DECLARES, not the columns present in the walk. The real ifEntry has 22 columns; a fixture tree with all 22 gives a horizontally-scrolled table with half the data off-frame and a lot of '-' cells wherever the walk is thin. Trim the tree's ifEntry to the ~12 columns you actually supply values for, and keep MibTable's column list identical so the two never disagree.

Type strings and value types are load-bearing for formatting. formatBySnmpType (utils/formatting.js) keys off the exact gosnmp names: 'TimeTicks' renders as '12d 7h 6m 23s (106,238,300)', anything numeric with |value| >= 10000 gets thousand separators, everything else falls through. A value sent as the STRING "3874192055" instead of the number still formats (Number() coerces) but a non-numeric string falls to JSON.stringify and appears in quotes. Counter32 values above 4294967296 are not wrong-looking to the UI but are wrong.

Enum decoding comes from ResolveOids, NOT from MibTable and NOT from the tree. formatValueWithEnum(value, oidInfoCache[oid], type) is what turns 6 into 'ethernetCsmacd(6)' and 2 into 'down(2)'. A stub that returns {} for ResolveOids leaves ifType/ifOperStatus as raw integers — the table still renders, so this failure is silent and easy to ship.

Async re-render, not a single paint: ResolveOids is awaited AFTER bulkResults is assigned, and MibTable/MibDecodeIndexes run in a reactive statement after the table view turns itself on. The table therefore paints at least three times (no names → names → decoded index columns). Wait for the network/microtask queue to settle (or poll for the decoded header text) before capturing, or you will screenshot the intermediate frame with 'Index' as the first header.

Toasts expire. notificationStore.add defaults to a 5000ms timeout, so 'Walk completed on 1 target(s), 144 results' is gone six seconds after the click. If you want the toast in frame, capture inside that window; if you do not, wait it out.

Settings decryption path: if any seeded credential begins with 'enc:', decryptSettings calls SettingsOpen, and a stub that throws blanks the in-memory community and flips credentialState to 'locked' (a banner in the Settings modal). If SettingsKeyStatus itself throws, the state becomes 'nostore'. Seed plaintext and return {available:true,...} and neither path runs. Also leave the legacy '_snmplens_ek' key unset — its presence triggers SettingsAdoptKey on boot.

MibTable resolving to null is tolerated but pointless: loadIndexes assigns tableInfo = null, the decode is skipped inside its own try/catch, and every row falls back to the italic raw-instance cell — visually identical to a decode failure. A rejected promise is handled the same way. Neither crashes; both quietly cost you the feature the shot is meant to show.

No canvas, no chart, no timestamp arithmetic anywhere in this panel — nothing here needs a live clock. The only date rendering is RecentHistory's formatTimestamp, which is hard-coded to toLocaleString('fr-FR') and prints dd/mm/yyyy regardless of the app locale; choose day-of-month > 12 so an English reader cannot misread it. Chrome headless also has no clipboard and no download sink: the copy buttons and the CSV/TXT/Table-CSV exports will throw if a scene clicks them.

ifTable has no RowStatus column (asserted by a Go test in pkg/mib/table_test.go), so the 'New row' bar and the delete-row context-menu entry cannot appear in an ifTable shot no matter what the fixture says. Row creation needs a different table whose MibTable answer includes rowStatusOid.

bindings.notes: THE binding for this panel. Awaited by mibStore.loadInternal, which reads `response.tree || []` and `response.diagnostics || []`, installs parent back-references, and sets {tree, isLoading:false}. Field-by-field truths verified against Go and gosmi v0.4.4, not guessed: (1) `access` is gosmi's Access.String() — CamelCase "ReadOnly" / "ReadWrite" / "NotAccessible" / "Notify" / "Unknown", NOT "read-only" (types/access_string.go:10). read-create also maps to "ReadWrite" (parser/object.go:50). NodeDetails prints the raw string, so "ReadOnly" is what appears on screen. (2) `mibType` is NodeKind.String(): Node | Scalar | Table | Row | Column | Notification | Group | Compliance | Capabilities | Unknown (types/nodekind_string.go). (3) `syntax` is Type.Name: an inline `INTEGER { up(1), down(2) }` becomes the literal "Enumeration" (smi/internal/module.go:646), a subtyped named type falls back to its parent's name so `DisplayString (SIZE(0..255))` is "DisplayString" (type.go:85 CreateType), base types render as "Integer32"/"ObjectIdentifier"/"Counter32"/"Gauge32"/"TimeTicks", and Table/Row nodes have NO type at all so syntax is the empty string "" (never "SEQUENCE OF IfEntry"). (4) `enumValues` is map[string]int64 → encoding/json sorts keys ALPHABETICALLY, so write them alphabetically to match a real capture. ifType's real enumValues is the entire IANAifType list (~126 named values in the bundled file); the 7 above are a deliberate trim — say so if fidelity matters. (5) plain OBJECT IDENTIFIER nodes (org/dod/internet/mgmt/mib-2/system/interfaces) carry description "", access "Unknown", mibType "Node" — this matches the committed screenshots/mib-browser.png exactly. (6) `iso` is NOT a node (it lives in gosmi's well-known module, not in any loaded module's GetNodes), so the tree has exactly TWO roots: zeroDotZero (0.0) and org (1.3), OID-sorted. (7) Descriptions arrive with the parser's whitespace normalisation applied: `(?:\r?\n *)+` collapsed to a single \n (parser/parser.go:39-46), so per-line indentation is gone but line breaks survive. Copy them verbatim from mibs/<FILE> and apply that collapse — the ones above are real IF-MIB/SNMPv2-MIB text, some trimmed at a sentence boundary. (8) `expanded` is NOT a Go field but IS honoured by TreeNode — see hazards; it is the only way to open the tree without clicking.

This is the single biggest 'used app' win in the panel: FavoritesPanel renders NOTHING when the array is empty, so an unseeded shot loses a whole card. NOTE: createFavoritesStore() calls load() at MODULE EVALUATION time, so this must be in localStorage before the bundle's first import runs — write it from a classic <script> in index.html, not from inside a module.

mibPathsStore (frontend/src/stores/mibPathsStore.js, STORAGE_KEY 'snmplens_paths'), loaded by App.svelte onMount. The outer keys MUST equal the string GetPersistentMibDirectory returns, byte for byte — they are used as map keys. Seeding is strictly optional for the tree (App.svelte immediately calls setDetectedMibs with whatever ListMibFiles returned, defaulting every unknown file to enabled), but it is the ONLY lever for the 'some MIBs switched off' state: set a value to false and that filename is dropped from the array passed to LoadMibsWithDiagnostics, which also changes the boot toast to '13 MIB(s) loaded successfully.'

App.svelte loadPanelWidth() — a plain integer string of pixels (default 350, no clamp applied on load; the 250..800 clamp only runs while dragging). 350 is too narrow once compact mode renders dotted paths: 'org.dod.internet' and 'ifTable.ifEntry (22)' wrap, and NodeDetails' 90px label column squeezes the description. 460 fits the deepest compact label and the Node Details rows without wrapping; go to 520 for the German locale.

App.svelte loadPanelWidth(); the literal string '1' collapses the panel to a 12px rail. Seed '0' for every scene that shows the tree. Seed '1' only for a scene deliberately showing the MIB editor or a wide Monitor grid with the rail tucked away.

settingsStore reads localStorage['settings'] at MODULE EVAL and merges over defaults, so it must also be written before the bundle loads. areas.visual:
Boot straight into the hero state with no clicks except one synthetic selection.

TREE SHAPE (set `expanded:true` in the fixture on exactly these nodes: org, dod, internet, mgmt, mib-2, interfaces, ifTable, ifEntry). Compact mode is ON by default, so what renders is: two roots — a bulleted leaf `zeroDotZero` and then `org.dod.internet`; under it the six internet children with `mgmt.mib-2 (15)`, `private.enterprises`, plus the leaves directory / experimental / security / snmpV2; under mib-2 the fifteen real groups (system, interfaces, ip, icmp, tcp, udp, transmission, snmp, host, ianaifType, `ifMIB.ifMIBObjects (6)`, ipMIB, tcpMIB, udpMIB, inetAddressMIB) with `interfaces` open, showing `ifNumber` and `ifTable.ifEntry (22)` opened onto all 22 columns. That is ~55 visible rows: deep, obviously a real MIB, and it scrolls inside .tree-container so the breadcrumb and Node Details stay pinned.

SELECTION: ifOperStatus (1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.8). It is the payoff node — the breadcrumb becomes a nine-segment trail `org › dod › internet › mgmt › mib-2 › interfaces › ifTable › ifEntry › ifOperStatus`, and Node Details fills every row it can: Name, OID `1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.8` in the mono chip with the copy button, Type badge `Column` (green), Syntax `Enumeration`, Access badge `ReadOnly` (blue), Parent `ifEntry`, and a four-line description. Selection is component-local, so the scene must do it after mount: `document.querySelector('[data-oid="1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.8"] .node-label').click()` — one click on a leaf selects without collapsing anything. ALTERNATIVE hero: click ifAdminStatus (…2.2.1.7) instead — same depth but Access `ReadWrite` renders the RED access badge, which is the more striking of the two and is the shot to use if the caption is about writable objects.

FAVOURITES: seed all five. The card sits between the breadcrumb and the tree with its star header reading "Favorites (5)" and five chips with per-type icons — it is the difference between "a MIB viewer" and "somebody's working install".

SEARCH SHOT (a second scene, worth its own image): set the input to `octets` via `el.value='octets'; el.dispatchEvent(new Event('input'))`. Three things appear at once that exist in no other state: the filter-chip row (Type: Scalar/Table/Column/Notification, Access: read-only/read-write), the tree pruned to the matching branches, and TreeNode's italic `description: …total number of octets received on the interface…` match snippets under the names — that snippet renderer only fires when the hit is in the description/syntax/enum rather than the name, so `octets` shows it and `ifIn` does not. Then click the `Column` chip to show one active (accent-filled) chip narrowing to columns.

DO NOT ship the panel with an empty tree, no favourites, 350px width and nothing selected: that is four separate empty states at once — no breadcrumb, no favourites card, no Node Details, and "No MIBs loaded." where the tree should be. It is roughly half the pixels of the rail.
hazards: Missing exports kill the whole app, not just this panel. stores/mibStore.js:2 imports LoadAllMibs and LoadEnabledMibs and never calls them; if screenshots/bridge/App.js drops either export, the ESM module graph throws 'does not provide an export named X' at eval and nothing renders. Keep every name the current placeholder exports.

The current placeholder bridge returns null from everything, which silently yields an EMPTY TREE by two different routes: (a) LoadMibsWithDiagnostics→null makes `response.tree` throw a TypeError inside mibStore's try/catch, landing on 'No MIBs loaded.'; (b) if ListMibFiles rejects, App.svelte's onMount try/catch swallows it and never calls mibStore.load() at all. Both fail with a plausible-looking empty panel and no console clue.

Returning a bare array from LoadMibsWithDiagnostics fails silently. mibStore reads `response.tree || []`, so an array (the shape LoadAllMibs uses) gives tree=[]. The wrapper object {tree, diagnostics} is mandatory.

Never put a `parent` key in the fixture, and never JSON.stringify the live tree. mibStore.addParentReferences walks the returned tree and assigns node.parent after load, making the object graph cyclic; Breadcrumb and NodeDetails' Parent row depend on it, so it must be the store that installs it.

`expanded` is the render lever and it is NOT a Go field — pkg/mib/service.go:16 has no such member, the frontend mutates it in place. Adding it to fixture nodes is what opens the tree on a plain page load. In COMPACT MODE (default on) the flag that matters is on the FIRST node of a single-child chain: TreeNode reads `node.expanded` but renders `endNode.children`, so org.expanded=true is what reveals internet's children, and mgmt.expanded=true is what reveals mib-2's. Setting it on the whole chain is harmless and mirrors what a click does.

Four pieces of visible state are component-local `let` bindings with no prop and no persistence, so localStorage cannot reach them: selectedNode (drives Breadcrumb AND the entire NodeDetails card), searchTerm (drives the filter-chip row and the match snippets), activeTypeFilters/activeAccessFilters, and compactMode. The scene bootstrap must drive them from the DOM after mount — `[data-oid="…"] .node-label`.click() for selection (data-oid is on every TreeNode, added for exactly this kind of lookup), and value+`new Event('input')` on `.search-bar input` for the search. Wait for the tree to exist first (MutationObserver or a rAF after the load promise settles) and give Chrome a --virtual-time-budget of ~2000ms.

A truncated fixture reads as an empty MIB. `children: []` renders the bullet leaf glyph instead of a chevron, so collapsed groups like ip/tcp/udp/snmp look like dead ends. Worse, in compact mode a node with EXACTLY ONE child is swallowed into its parent's label (`ip.ipForwarding`), which looks like a bug. Give every collapsed sibling at least TWO real children.

Wrong-looking-but-plausible field values to avoid: access is CamelCase ("ReadOnly", not "read-only") because NodeDetails prints the raw string; the syntax of an inline INTEGER enum is the literal "Enumeration" (not "INTEGER"); Table and Row nodes have syntax "" (not "SEQUENCE OF IfEntry") because gosmi leaves their Type nil; enumValues arrive alphabetically because encoding/json sorts map keys. Each of these is what a real capture would show and none of them is what you would guess.

NodeDetails renders rows for `selectedNode.status` and `selectedNode.units`, but the Go Node struct has neither field — those two rows are unreachable in the real app. Seeding them produces a screenshot of UI that cannot exist.

App.svelte calls mibStore.load(), not loadSilent(), so a green toast 'N MIB(s) loaded successfully.' appears on every boot and self-dismisses after 5000ms (stores/notifications.js). Decide deliberately: it makes the app look alive, but it also covers the top-right corner. Capture inside 5s to keep it, or past 5s to lose it.

favoritesStore and settingsStore both read localStorage during MODULE EVALUATION (favoritesStore's factory calls load() at the bottom; settingsStore does JSON.parse at the top level). Seeds written from inside a module — or from the stub bridge — can land too late. Put them in a classic, non-module <script> in the screenshot index.html.

GetPersistentMibDirectory's return value is a MAP KEY, not just a label: mibPathsStore indexes detectedMibs/enabledMibs by it. If the stub returns one string and the seeded snmplens_paths uses another (a stray trailing slash, or / vs \\), the enabled/disabled state is silently ignored. Define it once and share it across every scene.

Nothing in this panel needs a canvas, a timestamp range, a chart or a network fetch, and it subscribes to no runtime events — captures are deterministic. The one non-determinism is the boot toast's 5s timer.

areas.visual:
A static screenshot needs NO runtime events: seed everything through MonitorLoadSessionData and let the chart draw once (animation is off, so frame one is final). Emit monitor:samples only for an animated GIF; note the subscription is registered at pollingStore module eval, so events fired before the store's set(loaded) at t~300ms are dropped (the update() maps over an empty array).

DATA SET FOR THE HERO SHOT — session A, "Core switches - CPU load", id 7c1f9a24..., 3 targets, ONE OID (hrProcessorLoad.1, Gauge32), 60s interval, 24 h => 1440 ticks x 3 targets = 4320 DataPoints. Threshold {max: 80, forSeconds: 120}. viewMode 'raw' (mandatory: threshold bands are drawn only when mode === 'raw'), windowMs 0 ("All" -> the full 24 h arc), zeroBased true, height 300.
  tick k in [0,1440), ts = new Date(T0 + k*60000).toISOString() with T0 = (now - 24h) floored to the minute. THE SAME STRING FOR ALL THREE TARGETS.
  base(k) = 46 + 20*sin(2*PI*(k-380)/1440)   // one diurnal hump, trough ~04:00, peak ~16:00
  Core-SW-01: base + N(0,2.5), offset -6   Core-SW-02: base + N(0,2.5), offset -9   Edge-RTR-Paris: base + N(0,3), offset +4
  Incident 1 (resolved, mid-chart): k in [880,940) add a ramp on Core-SW-02 up to 89, back under 80 by k=940. -> threshold.opened at k=882, threshold.resolved at k=940. Visible as a red dashed rule at 80, the whole area above it tinted #d03b3b1a, and the curve poking through it.
  Incident 2 (still open at the right edge): k in [1395,1440) ramp Edge-RTR-Paris to 86-92 and LEAVE IT THERE. That makes MetricTiles paint its tile red (classify() runs on the LAST value only) while the other two stay normal — a red tile plus two calm ones reads far better than three of either.
  Outage: k in [790,798) (8 minutes) set value/delta/rate = null, error "request timeout (after 1 retries)", responseTimeMs 5000 on ALL THREE targets. Produces a grey outage band (chartChrome().muted + '33'), three broken lines (spanGaps:false), and justifies a reachability.down/reachability.up pair on the alert timeline.
  responseTimeMs: 9-26 ms normally, 60-140 ms across the incident-2 window (the latency companion chart, showLatency=true, then shows a real correlated bump instead of a flat line).

SESSION B, "WAN uplink - Paris", id 1a2b7f60..., 2 OIDs (ifInOctets.2 / ifOutOctets.2, Counter64) x 2 targets = 4 series, layout 'stacked', viewMode 'rate', windowMs 3600000. Stacked is the most impressive layout in the app: one plot, four curves, alternating left/right y-axes each TINTED with its series colour, a legend box (it appears only once datasetCount > 1), and axis titles carrying the resolved MIB name. `value` must be a plausible monotonically-rising cumulative octet count (~8.8e11) and `rate` the octets/s you actually want plotted (2.5e6 trough to 2.2e7 peak, with one 6-minute spike to 5.4e7 around 40 min before the edge — min-max decimation is specifically there to preserve a one-sample spike, so make it worth preserving). Rate is what the axis shows; value is only read in 'raw'.

SESSION C, "UPS battery - Salle B", stopped, collapsed: true. Costs ~40px, and proves the panel handles many sessions — a card in the Stopped state with a Resume button, its charts unmounted.

ALERT TIMELINE (bottom of every expanded graph-mode card): return 12-16 events from EventsQuery for session A. Composition that looks best: 4 threshold.opened (state 'open', severity 'major' — these are the ONLY ones that get a red mark on the strip, `openings = incidents.filter(e => e.state !== 'resolved')`), 4 threshold.resolved (state 'resolved' — rendered dimmed with a green check, which is what makes the list read as an incident history rather than an alarm dump), 1 reachability.down + 1 reachability.up matching the outage, plus 2-3 older threshold pairs. Every ev.ts MUST fall inside [first, last] of session.results or strip() clamps the mark to 0% or 100% and they pile up at one edge. Keep incidents.length above 12 so the "+N more alert(s)" footer shows.

TIMESTAMP RECENCY: the x axis itself does NOT need "now" — it is built from the data's own max (latestX()), so a 2024 data set renders identically. Generate relative to capture time anyway: the alert list prints absolute local timestamps via formatTimestamp, the stats grid prints firstTimestamp/lastTimestamp, and a "LIVE" pulsing dot over week-old data is the kind of detail a reader notices.

MAKE SURE THESE ARE NOT DEFAULT-EMPTY: the setup form (needs settings.targets + snpMonitorView.form, else it is a blank box saying "configure at least one target"); the MIB tree (else every OID is a raw dotted string in the header, the axis titles, the tiles and the alert rows); the alert timeline (renders NOTHING at all when incidents is empty — {#if incidents.length}); the target chips row. Deliberately DO leave the stats grid and the historical block closed unless the harness can click, since neither can be opened from localStorage.
hazards: MODULE LINK FAILURE, the top risk: these are static named imports and a missing export blanks the ENTIRE app, not just this panel. wailsjs/go/main/App must export at minimum MonitorCreateSession, MonitorStart, MonitorStop, MonitorRunning, MonitorSaveDataPoints, MonitorLoadSessions, MonitorLoadSessionData, MonitorDeleteSession (pollingStore), MonitorGetStats, MonitorLoadHistoricalData, MonitorLoadBuckets (MonitorPanel), EventsQuery (AlertTimeline), SettingsSeal/SettingsOpen/SettingsAdoptKey/SettingsKeyStatus/SettingsForgetKey (crypto.js, pulled in by settingsStore). wailsjs/runtime/runtime must export EventsOn — and EventsOn must RETURN A FUNCTION, since AlertTimeline calls the result on destroy (it does guard with typeof, but nothing else does).

THE 5-MINUTE WINDOW. MonitorChart defaults windowMs = 300000 and follow = true, and applyWindow() pins x.min = latestX() - windowMs. Seed 24 h of samples without setting chartOpts[sessionId].windowMs and the screenshot shows the last five minutes: a nearly flat line, no diurnal shape, no spike, no outage. Set windowMs to 0 (whole buffer) or 3600000. TIMEBASES = [60000, 300000, 900000, 3600000, 0].

ZERO-WIDTH MOUNT KILLS THE CHART PERMANENTLY. create() bails when `!parent || parent.clientWidth === 0`, and it is only ever called from a single requestAnimationFrame; every retry path (`$: if (chart && ...) refresh()`, the structure-change block, the theme block) is guarded on `chart` being non-null. So if the canvas's parent has no layout at that first frame the chart never appears and never recovers. The Monitor tab must be the ACTIVE tab (App.svelte mounts panels behind {#if activeTab === 'monitor'} — activeTab is a plain `let`, not persisted; drive it with stores/tabRequest requestTab('monitor'), a synthetic Ctrl+4 keydown, or a scene shim) and the viewport must be sized before load. Never pre-mount the panel hidden.

THE COUNTER AUTO-SWITCH. MonitorPanel has a reactive block that sets viewModes[id] = 'rate' the first time any result carries a snmpType matching /counter/i, if the mode is still 'raw'. It fires AFTER your seeded viewModes are read. A Counter session you wanted in raw mode silently becomes a rate chart — and thresholdTargets() returns [] unless mode === 'raw', so the red band, the tint and the 'max 80' label vanish. Seed view.autoModeApplied[sessionId] = true to disable it.

THRESHOLD BANDS ARE RAW-MODE ONLY, and MetricTiles' red `outOfRange` state likewise (`m === 'raw' && classify(...)`). A rate/delta/latency chart can never show a threshold line. Put the band on a Gauge32 session in raw mode.

TIMESTAMP IDENTITY PER TICK. outageRanges() buckets points by Date.parse(timestamp) and calls a tick an outage when failed === total. Give each target its own slightly-offset timestamp and every bucket holds one point, so ANY single failed sample paints a grey outage band across the plot. The real scheduler stamps once per tick (scheduler.go:147) — fixtures must too.

MISSING `oid` ON DATA POINTS. Every filter in the panel is `(r.oid || session.oid) === oid` (MonitorChart.forOid, buildStacked, MetricTiles.buildTiles). Omit `oid` on a multi-OID session's points and they all collapse onto the first facet, leaving the second chart/axis empty. Single-OID sessions may omit it.

UNIT LABELS ARE NOT WHAT snmpUnits.js SUGGESTS. inferUnit() is called with the NUMERIC OID everywhere (MonitorChart line ~120, MetricTiles, buildStacked), never the resolved MIB name, so OCTET_RE (/octets|bytes|bandwidth/) and PERCENT_RE (/percent|pct|utili|usage|load/) can never match. Expect a bare '/s' axis in rate mode and an unlabelled axis in raw mode — you will NOT get 'bit/s' or '%'. The only type-driven branches that do fire are TimeTicks (label 'durée', a French string in the English UI) and mode === 'latency' ('ms'). Values are still scaled with k/M/G suffixes, so pick magnitudes that exercise that.

TRANSIENT STATE THAT localStorage CANNOT REACH: sessionStats, historicalResults/historicalBuckets/historicalInfo, loadingHistory, channelsFor, visibleRanges, openThreshold and MonitorChart's `fullscreen` are all plain `let`s reinitialised at mount. The stats grid, the historical chart block, the channel-picker modal and the open threshold editor therefore CANNOT appear on a passive page load — each needs a real click (and, for the historical block, a click plus the MonitorLoadBuckets round trip). Budget those into the scene script if you want them in a shot.

TIMING. pollingStore fires initFromBackend from setTimeout(..., 300) at module eval, then awaits MonitorLoadSessions, then MonitorLoadSessionData sequentially per session, then MonitorRunning; only after that does the panel have data, and MonitorChart draws one rAF later. AlertTimeline adds one EventsQuery per card. Give the capture at least ~1500 ms (--virtual-time-budget=3000 is safer) and make the stub's promises resolve, not hang.

MonitorLoadSessions THROWING is caught with a console.warn and an early return — silent empty panel, no error UI. Same for MonitorLoadSessionData (per session, points stay []) and MonitorRunning (everything reads Stopped). A stub that rejects produces a plausible-looking but empty screenshot rather than a visible failure.

CHART.JS NEEDS THE CSS VARIABLES. chartChrome() reads --text-color/--text-muted/--border-color/--bg-light-color off document.documentElement at chart-creation time and falls back to dark hex literals. Capture with the stylesheet applied and the theme attribute settled, or the axes/gridlines get dark defaults on a light page. Also: seriesColor() takes `dark = theme !== 'light'` from the prop, while isDarkTheme() reads data-theme off the root — keep settings.theme and the root attribute consistent.

chartjs-plugin-zoom and chartjs-adapter-date-fns are hard imports of MonitorChart; the x scale is type:'time' and will not render without the adapter. Chart.js 4.5 + a real <canvas> is required — headless Chrome is fine, but any offscreen/zero-size container is not (see the zero-width hazard).

AlertTimeline renders literally nothing when incidents is empty, and the strip marks need session.results non-empty (strip() returns [] otherwise). An events fixture that ignores filter.sessionId will splash the same alerts under every session card, which reads as a bug in the shot.

settings.polling.autoResume === true makes reconcileWithScheduler call MonitorStart on every stopped session with results, briefly flipping cards to Running and back if the stub rejects. Keep it false and control the Running state through MonitorRunning alone.

MAX_SERIES is 8 (chartPalette.js). Past 8 targets on one OID chart the extras are dropped and a yellow 'N more target(s) not plotted' footnote appears — fine as a deliberate detail, bad as an accident. Keep 2-4 targets per session.

areas.visual:
TRAPS SCENE. Seed 14 traps in `trapHistory` with `traps.persist: true`, spread over the last ~40 minutes so the Time column shows distinct times. The mix that tells the story: 5 linkDown/linkUp pairs from two routers (the flapping interface an operator actually chases), 1 coldStart, 1 authenticationFailure, 1 SNMPv1 trap (proves v1 support and shows the five synthesised varbinds), 2 enterprise traps from the UPS at 10.20.4.23 — one of them an INFORM, because the Inform badge renders ORANGE against the accent-blue Trap badge and that contrast is the single most legible thing in the row (Trap.svelte .pdu-type-badge.inform). Then: (a) call trapStore.start() after mount so the header button reads 'Stop Listening', the Traps tab shows the green '●' and the '14' badge, and the top line reads 'Listening for traps on port 162'; (b) EXPAND the first row — a click on .trap-summary, or dispatch it — because the collapsed list is six columns of text while the expanded row is the four-column Name/OID/Type/Value varbind table, which is the panel's whole point. Expanding the linkDown gives sysUpTime rendered as a human duration (formatBySnmpType turns TimeTicks 184203451 into '21d 7h 47m (184,203,451)'), ifDescr 'GigabitEthernet0/3', ifOperStatus 2. The open row also paints accent-blue with white text, which anchors the shot. Leave the Send-Trap form COLLAPSED for the main capture (it is 5 rows of form and pushes the list off-screen); if you want it, make it a second scene with sendTarget prefilled and two varbinds added. Leave the filter bar at its defaults — the counter then reads '14 / 14' and the CSV/JSON export buttons appear (they are hidden when filteredTraps is empty, and an empty list is what an unused app looks like).

EVENTS SCENE. Return ~22 items from EventsQuery with nextCursor set to the last item's seq and total 1284 — that gives '1284 matching' on the right, a 'Load more' button at the foot, and the impression of months of history rather than a demo. Composition, top to bottom, all within the last ~5 hours: 8 trap rows (minor, grey-brown left border, each with payloadSize > 0 so the details button shows), 3 threshold.opened (major, orange border) each followed further down by its threshold.resolved (info, sharing the same corrId), 1 reachability.down still open (major) and 1 reachability.up (info), 1 system.sink_dead_letter (major) and 1 system.info. Leave roughly a third of them acked:true — an acked row renders at opacity 0.55 with a green tick, and that visual gradient between fresh and handled alarms is what makes the list read as WORKED rather than dumped. Counts: unacked 23, so the tab carries a red 23 badge, the title carries the '23 unacknowledged' pill, and unackedByCategory puts a small red number on the Trap / Threshold / Reachability / System chips. Two deliberate interactions if the harness can click: select 2-3 rows to raise the accent-tinted bulk bar ('3 selected · Acknowledge · Delete'), which proves the list is interactive; and for a second variant, open a trap row's payload modal — a 6-varbind JSON body pretty-printed in the monospace textarea. Seed `settings.targets` with '# label' suffixes so the Source column reads core-sw-01 / edge-rtr-paris / ups-dc1, and make sure the MIB tree is loaded so the OID column reads 'ifInOctets.3' and 'linkDown' rather than raw digits. Do NOT turn on Anonymous Mode for either shot — it replaces every source with 'Device-1' and every param inside the title too.
hazards: DOUBLE event:new SUBSCRIPTION. App.svelte's onMount calls eventsStore.listen() and EventsPanel's onMount calls it AGAIN (EventsPanel.svelte:42). Each call registers another EventsOn('event:new') handler, so one emitted event is prepended TWICE with the same ev.id into a keyed {#each} — duplicate keys, plus a double increment of the unacked count and a double toast from announce(). In a dev build Svelte throws 'Cannot have duplicate keys in a keyed each'; in the prod Vite build it corrupts the list silently. Make the Events scene entirely static (EventsQuery + EventsCounts) and never emit event:new while the Events tab is mounted. This is a pre-existing app bug, not a stub artefact.

MISSING BINDING EXPORTS KILL THE WHOLE TAB, not just a feature. Module-level `import { SendTrap, SendInform } from '../wailsjs/go/main/App'` in TrapPanel.svelte and `import { EventsQuery, EventsCounts, EventsAck, EventsAckAll, EventsDelete, EventsClear }` in eventsStore.js are ES imports: an absent export is a load-time failure ('does not provide an export named X'), and the panel never renders. The stub must export every one of those plus StartTrapListener, StopTrapListener, GetOidDetails and EventsPayload even though most are never called.

i18n PLACEHOLDERS THAT ARE NOT SUPPLIED RENDER AS LITERAL BRACES. renderTitle passes ev.params (or {}) to svelte-i18n; a missing ICU argument makes format() throw, svelte-i18n catches it (node_modules/svelte-i18n/dist/runtime.cjs:537) and returns the RAW message — so a threshold.opened without heldSeconds shows '... (held {heldSeconds}s)' on screen. Every fixture event must carry every placeholder its key names in frontend/src/i18n/en.json under events.kind.*. Two real kinds get this wrong in production and should be kept OUT of the shot: system.mib_load_failed (key needs {file}, recordSystemEvent at app_service.go:210 records no params at all) and operation.failed (key needs {operation} and {target}, app.go:291 records none). system.sink_dead_letter is the one system kind that does carry full params (app.go:801) and renders correctly.

system.info ALWAYS READS 'Service notice'. Its en.json entry has no placeholders, so renderTitle returns the translation and the useful text in `summary` is only ever the tooltip. Fine as one quiet row, useless as the system representative — pair it with system.sink_dead_letter.

THE VERSION FILTER CANNOT MATCH. handleTrap sets version from gosnmp's SnmpVersion.String(), which returns '1', '2c' or '3' (verified at gosnmp@v1.43.2/helper.go:902) — but TrapPanel's version <select> offers the values 'SNMPv1', 'SNMPv2c', 'SNMPv3', and Trap.svelte:38 tests `t.version === 'SNMPv1'`. So the fixture must use '1'/'2c'/'3' (that is what the app really receives, and the Version column reads fine), and the scene must NEVER pre-set filterVersion or every row disappears. Existing app bug; do not paper over it with 'SNMPv2c' fixtures that could not come from the backend.

isListening IS NOT PERSISTED ANYWHERE. There is no localStorage key and no setter on trapStore. The green '●', the 'Stop Listening' label and the 'Waiting for traps...' empty text all depend on it, and the ONLY way in is trapStore.start() -> await StartTrapListener(). That also fires a 5-second success toast (stores/notifications.js:11) — capture after 5.5 s or keep the toast on purpose.

THE TRAPS TAB BADGE AND THE EVENTS BADGE APPEAR ON EVERY SCENE. trapStore is imported by App.svelte for the badge, so loadPersistedTraps() runs at app boot on all scenes, and App.svelte's onMount always calls EventsCounts. Seeding trapHistory or a non-zero unacked count leaks '14' and a red '23' into the Operations, Monitor and Discovery screenshots too. That is probably desirable (a busy install), but it must be a deliberate choice, not a surprise.

GetOidDetails IS AWAITED PER VARBIND AND THE MESSAGE COLUMN IS EMPTY UNTIL IT RESOLVES. Trap.svelte's `$: resolveTrap(trap)` clears mainTrapMessage to '' and only then awaits. 14 rows x ~6 varbinds is roughly 100 promises resolving after mount; capture after they settle or the widest column of the Traps panel is blank. If the stub rejects or omits the OID, the fallback is the bare numeric OID, which looks like a broken MIB install.

THE TRAP OID VALUES CARRY A LEADING DOT. gosnmp yields Name/ObjectIdentifier values as '.1.3.6.1...' (confirmed by the comments at pkg/snmp/trap.go:232 and pkg/snmp/client.go:308). Trap.svelte strips it before calling GetOidDetails, but the journal stores it unstripped in ev.oid and dedupKey. So the GetOidDetails stub should key on the STRIPPED form while the events fixture keeps the dot — resolveOidDisplay strips it again on the Events side.

NO CANVAS, NO CHARTS, NO TIMESTAMP MATH in either panel — both are plain DOM lists, which makes them the safest two panels in the app to stub. The only date handling is Trap.svelte's toLocaleTimeString() and formatTimestamp(), which is hardcoded to 'fr-FR' (utils/formatting.js:8) and therefore renders '05/09/2026 14:41:07' in the Events ts column regardless of the chosen locale. Feed valid RFC3339 or that column reads 'Invalid Date'.

EventsQuery MUST RESOLVE, NOT REJECT. A rejection leaves items empty and the panel shows 'No events yet. Traps and threshold breaches will appear here.' — the exact 'unused app' look the harness exists to avoid. Same for the shape: the store reads page.items / page.total / page.nextCursor, so resolving with an array instead of an object silently yields an empty list.
EventsPayload RESOLVES TO A STRING, not an object — it goes straight into the textarea. Returning an object renders '[object Object]'.

ANONYMOUS MODE IS FORCED OFF ON LOAD (settingsStore.js:69) and is intentionally non-persistent. If a scene wants the anonymised variant it has to flip it in-memory after boot (Ctrl+Shift+A) — seeding anonymousMode:true in localStorage will not work, and should not be made to.

areas.visual:
HISTORY — the list shot. Seed LoadHistory with 26–30 entries so pagination appears (PAGE_SIZE is 20, HistoryPanel.svelte:22 — the pager only renders above 20, and "SNMP History (28 entries)" in the H3 with a "1 / 2" pager is the single strongest signal of a used install). Mix: ~10 WALK (ifTable 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2, ipAddrTable 1.3.6.1.2.1.4.20, tcpConnTable 1.3.6.1.2.1.6.13, entPhysicalTable), ~8 GET (sysDescr .0, sysUpTime .0, ifOperStatus.3), 3 GETBULK, 2 SET (ifAdminStatus with value "2"/valueType "Integer" — SET entries expose the extra Value/Type detail rows), 2 GETNEXT, and 3 FAILURES with success:false plus error:"connect failed: request timeout (after 1 retries)" or "walk failed: no response from 10.20.0.44" — the red "Error" badge and the red X give the list contrast, and the operation filter/status filter above it stop looking decorative. Timestamps spread over the last ~6 hours descending, durations 12ms–4.2s (formatDuration switches to "4.20s" above 1000ms, so include both forms). Give one entry targets:["10.20.0.11","10.20.0.12","10.20.0.13"] so the "3 target(s)" column is not "1 target(s)" all the way down. A populated $mibStore.tree is what turns the name column from raw OIDs into ifTable / sysDescr — without it the whole column reads as digits and the panel looks like a packet log.

HISTORY — the money shot is the DIFF. Two WALK entries, same OID 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2, same target 10.20.0.11, 4h33m apart (A 09:14:22, B 13:47:05). Per interface emit four varbinds: .1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.2.i (ifDescr, OctetString), .8.i (ifOperStatus, Integer), .10.i (ifInOctets, Counter32), .16.i (ifOutOctets, Counter32).
A holds ifIndex 1–4: 1 GigabitEthernet0/1 up in 88123456 out 44210987 | 2 GigabitEthernet0/2 up in 12983440 out 9114320 | 3 GigabitEthernet0/3 DOWN(2) in 0 out 0 | 4 GigabitEthernet0/4 up in 5512900 out 4410233.
B holds ifIndex 1,2,3,5: 1 up in 91004872 out 46882301 | 2 up in 13470115 out 9552008 | 3 now UP(1) in 41288 out 30991 | 5 TenGigabitEthernet1/1 up in 2201455 out 1980662.
That yields exactly: 3 identical (the three unchanged ifDescr), 7 modified (two counters on if1, two on if2, operStatus + two counters on if3), 4 added (the whole if5 row), 4 removed (the whole if4 row) — 18 rows total, 15 visible with "Show identical rows" off. Every one of the four stat colours in the diff header is non-zero, the modal shows green/red/amber bands together, and the story reads instantly: an SFP was swapped for a 10G uplink and a down port came back. Header labels render as "A: WALK 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2 @ 09:14:22" / "B: … @ 13:47:05", so set TZ in the capture environment or the two times drift.

DISCOVERY — scan tab. Put 10.20.0.0/27 in the CIDR box, not the default 192.168.1.0/24: expandCIDR drops network and broadcast, so a /27 is exactly 30 addresses, and returning 30 rows makes the "9 reachable / 30 total" line arithmetically true and fills the 500px table without a scrollbar swallowing half the shot. A /24 forces either 254 rows or a number that contradicts itself. Nine reachable, sorted by IP: two ISR4331 routers (.1 .2), a Catalyst 2960X, an EX2300-48P, an Aruba 2930F (.11 .12 .13), an ESXi host and a Debian NAS (.20 .21), an APC AP9631 UPS (.24), an HP LaserJet M507dn (.30). Nine green-tinted rows scattered through 21 half-opacity timeout rows is what a real sweep looks like; a solid block of green does not. The sysDescr column is the row that sells it — real vendor banners with version and build strings, ellipsised at 300px with the full text in the title attribute.

DISCOVERY — ping tab. Target 10.20.0.1, count 8, 8/8 received, 0% loss, min 0.712 / avg 1.104 / max 2.318, and eight `replies` so the raw-output <pre> shows a real eight-line block rather than the empty box the code comment complains about. If you want the red loss styling instead, use received 7 / lossPercent 12.5.

DISCOVERY — traceroute tab. Twelve hops to 8.8.8.8 as above: LAN gateway, CGNAT, transit, one fully-starred hop 5, a partial star on hop 11, arriving at 8.8.8.8 around 20ms. RTTs climbing monotonically with realistic jitter across the three columns is what separates this from placeholder data.

Anonymous Mode is worth one extra shot of the discovery table (IPs become Device-1…, sysName Host-1…, sysDescr masked), but it cannot be seeded — see the hazards.
hazards: THE BIG ONE — neither panel's interesting state is reachable from localStorage. HistoryPanel's expandedIds, diffMode, diffSelectionA/B, showDiffModal, selectMode, searchTerm, sortKey and currentPage are all plain component-local `let`s (HistoryPanel.svelte:23–56). DiscoveryPanel's activeSubTab, results, pingResult, traceHops, showOnlyReachable are the same (DiscoveryPanel.svelte:12–31). Nothing reads a URL or a store for any of them. So a pure page load screenshots: History = the entry list only, collapsed, no diff; Discovery = the CIDR form over the 'No scan results.' empty state, on the Discovery sub-tab. The diff modal, the results table, the ping stats and the traceroute table CANNOT be reached by seeding.

Consequence: the scene runner needs a DOM seam, and the stub bridge module is the right place for it — `wailsjs/go/main/App.js` is imported before the app mounts, so it can read the scene query param and schedule DOM actions on a timer, with Chrome given --virtual-time-budget (or a --timeout) rather than a bare --screenshot. Selectors that exist today: Discovery sub-tabs are `.sub-tabs .sub-tab` in order Discovery/Ping/Traceroute; the scan button is the `.form-row .btn.btn-primary`; inputs are #discovery-cidr, #ping-target, #ping-count, #trace-target. History: the Diff Mode button is the 2nd `.header-actions .btn.tertiary`, entry rows carry `data-entry-id`, and the Compare button only renders once both A and B are chosen. Nothing here has a stable test id — if the harness is allowed one source change, adding data-scene attributes to those controls is cheaper than maintaining nth-child selectors.

bind:value inputs will not accept a programmatic assignment. Setting el.value on #discovery-cidr / #ping-target / #trace-target does not update the Svelte variable — the shim must dispatch `new Event('input')` after assigning, or the scan runs against the default 192.168.1.0/24 and the CIDR shown contradicts the results.

Missing EXPORTS crash the whole app, not just the panel. historyStore.js names six bindings at module scope (SaveHistoryEntry, LoadHistory, DeleteHistoryEntry, DeleteHistoryEntries, ClearHistory, ImportHistoryEntries) and crypto.js names five (SettingsSeal, SettingsOpen, SettingsAdoptKey, SettingsKeyStatus, SettingsForgetKey) — an ES module missing any one throws 'does not provide an export named X' at import time and nothing renders. Five of the six history bindings are never CALLED during a screenshot; they still must exist. Same for wailsjs/runtime/runtime: EventsOn, EventsOff, OnFileDrop, OnFileDropOff.

LoadHistory is awaited but its result is merged, not assigned blindly. historyStore.init() re-merges anything already in the store (historyStore.js:66) — harmless, but if the stub resolves LoadHistory synchronously-ish and something else has already pushed entries you get duplicates by id.

A populated MIB tree silently changes what an expanded WALK renders. ResultsDisplay decides raw-vs-table exactly once per result set (ResultsDisplay.svelte:565): if $mibStore.tree contains ifTable it auto-switches to TABLE view and fires MibTable + MibDecodeIndexes. Stub those two and the expanded entry is a proper pivoted ifTable with decoded ifIndex; leave them throwing and it degrades to raw instances (ugly, not broken); return an empty tree and you get the raw varbind list instead. Pick deliberately — this is the difference between a screenshot that shows off conceptual tables and one that shows a flat OID dump.

DiffModal only recognises WalkResponse / GetBulkResponse. buildOidMap branches on result.type being exactly one of those strings (DiffModal.svelte:20); anything else is wrapped as a single [res.result] and the diff collapses to one row. And isDiffEligible (HistoryPanel.svelte:243) only lets WALK/GETBULK entries be selected at all — a GET entry's diff checkbox renders dashed and disabled.

sysUpTime is not a duration. Discovery's sysUpTime is a string holding raw TimeTicks centiseconds ('1099992310'), because formatSnmpValue returns an int64 for TimeTicks and discovery.go formats it with %v. There is no formatTimeTicks on this path. A fixture reading '127d 3h 46m' would be visibly impossible.

PingResult has no `output` field — the comment at DiscoveryPanel.svelte:286 exists because a previous version rendered a permanently empty box from exactly that mistake. The pre block is fed by `replies`, an array of NUMBERS (ms.toFixed(2) is called on each); strings throw.
Traceroute RTTs are strings with the unit baked in ('13.402 ms', or '*'), not numbers. hop.ip === '' renders as '*'. Passing numbers gives unitless cells.

Anonymous Mode cannot be seeded. settingsStore.js:67 forces anonymousMode=false on every load, deliberately (documented in CLAUDE.md as non-persistent by design). An Anonymous-Mode shot needs a click on the header toggle after mount — and the anonymize maps are per-session counters, so the labels (Device-1, Host-1) depend on the order rows are first rendered.

No canvas, no chart, no real-timestamp arithmetic in either panel — both are plain tables. The only time-dependent rendering is formatTimestamp/formatLabel, which use toLocaleString('fr-FR') and toLocaleTimeString(); fix TZ and the container locale or the diff labels and the history timestamps shift between runs and the images churn in git.

The History clear/export/confirm modals (HistoryExportModal, ConfirmDialog) and the DiffModal all render with position:fixed overlays at z-index 1000 — they cover the panel entirely, so a diff shot is a shot of the modal, not of the modal over a visible list. Plan two separate captures rather than one.

DiscoveryPanel's addToTargets / addAllReachable call settingsStore.save(), which calls encryptSettings → SettingsSeal. If the scene shim clicks '+ Target' the stub needs SettingsSeal to resolve; a rejection is caught and only warns, but the notification toast that follows will be in the shot.

areas.visual:
WHAT THE SHOT MUST SHOW: a real vendor MIB open, syntax-coloured, with two red squiggles on screen, a fix bar offering to repair the IMPORTS clause, and a five-row problems list underneath naming the line, the message and the diagnostic code. Nothing here needs a click.

=== 1. THE FILE (verbatim; this is the `content` of MibEditorRead and the editor buffer) ===
Name it ACME-POE-MIB. 90 lines (the last is empty after the trailing newline), 2469 bytes as the edited buffer. Line numbers below are load-bearing — every diagnostic position was derived from this exact text.

ACME-POE-MIB DEFINITIONS ::= BEGIN

IMPORTS
    MODULE-IDENTITY, OBJECT-TYPE, Integer32, Gauge32, Counter32, TimeTicks,
    enterprises                    FROM SNMPv2-SMI
    DisplayString                  FROM SNMPv2-TC;

acmePoeMIB MODULE-IDENTITY
    LAST-UPDATED "202608140000Z"
    ORGANIZATION "Acme Networks"
    CONTACT-INFO "noc@acme.example"
    DESCRIPTION  "Power sourcing equipment on the ACME-4800 series."
    ::= { enterprises 41112 4 }

acmePoeObjects OBJECT IDENTIFIER ::= { acmePoeMIB 1 }   -- power sourcing subtree

acmePoeDraw OBJECT-TYPE
    SYNTAX      Integerr32
    UNITS       "milliwatts"
    MAX-ACCESS  read-only
    STATUS      current
    DESCRIPTION
        "Power the attached powered devices are drawing right now."
    ::= { acmePoeObjects 1 }

acmePoeFaults OBJECT-TYPE
    SYNTAX      Counter32
    MAX-ACCESS  read-only
    STATUS      current
    DESCRIPTION
        "Overload and short-circuit faults since the switch last restarted."
    ::= { acmePoeObjects 1 }

acmePoePortTable OBJECT-TYPE
    SYNTAX      SEQUENCE OF AcmePoePortEntry
    MAX-ACCESS  not-accessible
    STATUS      current
    DESCRIPTION
        "One row per PoE-capable port, indexed as in ifTable."
    ::= { acmePoeObjects 2 }

acmePoePortEntry OBJECT-TYPE
    SYNTAX      AcmePoePortEntry
    MAX-ACCESS  read-only
    STATUS      current
    DESCRIPTION
        "PoE state of one port."
    INDEX   { ifIndex }
    ::= { acmePoePortTable 1 }

AcmePoePortEntry ::= SEQUENCE {
    acmePoePortEnable   TruthValue,
    acmePoePortClass    Integer32,
    acmePoePortDraw     Gauge32,
    acmePoePortLabel    DisplayString
}

acmePoePortEnable OBJECT-TYPE
    SYNTAX      TruthValue
    MAX-ACCESS  read-write
    STATUS      current
    DESCRIPTION
        "Whether this port is allowed to supply power."
    ::= { acmePoePortEntry 1 }

acmePoePortClass OBJECT-TYPE
    SYNTAX      Integer32 (0..8)
    MAX-ACCESS  read-only
    STATUS      current
    DESCRIPTION
        "The IEEE 802.3af/at class the attached device negotiated."
    ::= { acmePoePortEntry 2 }

acmePoePortDraw OBJECT-TYPE
    SYNTAX      Gauge32
    UNITS       "milliwatts"
    MAX-ACCESS  read-only
    STATUS      current
    DESCRIPTION
        "Power this port is delivering right now."
    ::= { acmePoePortEntry 3 }

acmePoePortLabel OBJECT-TYPE
    SYNTAX      DisplayString (SIZE (0..64))
    MAX-ACCESS  read-write
    STATUS      current
    ::= { acmePoePortEntry 4 }

END

=== 2. WHY THIS TEXT (every problem is real, not invented) ===
- line 18 col 17 `Integerr32` — a typo for Integer32. Two effects at once: the tokeniser does NOT colour it (it is not in tokenize.js TYPES, so it renders plain grey between two blue-coloured neighbours) AND the analyser underlines it in red. The mark width is cw x len(symbol) = exactly the 10 characters of the token.
- line 32 col 11 — acmePoeFaults repeats `{ acmePoeObjects 1 }`, the classic copy-paste. The underline starts at the `acmePoeObjects` token (Oid.Pos is the first sub-identifier, not the brace) and is 13 chars wide against a 14-char token: it sits under the OID almost exactly.
- line 43 col 5 (warning) — acmePoePortEntry is a conceptual row with MAX-ACCESS read-only.
- line 83 col 1 (warning) — acmePoePortLabel has no DESCRIPTION.
- line 4 col 5 (info) — TimeTicks imported and never used. Info severity is listed but never underlined.
- lines 48 and 52 — ifIndex and TruthValue are used and never imported, which is what fills the fix bar. Both are in the catalogue, so they are missing IMPORTS rather than unknown types.
Net: status pill reads "2 error(s)" in red; the problems list has exactly 5 rows, which is what its 150px max-height holds without scrolling.

=== 3. HOW TO GET THERE WITHOUT CLICKING (order matters) ===
The editor opens no file by default: with source === null the whole pane is a centred book icon and "Pick a MIB on the left, or open a file, to start editing." That is the failure mode to avoid, and no localStorage key fixes it — the open state must be driven programmatically.

BEFORE the app mounts (in main.js, inside setupI18n().then, above `new App(...)`):
  a) `requestTab('mibeditor')` from src/stores/tabRequest.js — App.svelte:255 picks it up in its first update cycle, so MibEditorPanel is in the FIRST render.
  b) `mibEditorStore.openSource(SOURCE)` where SOURCE is the MibEditorRead shape above (clean copy: line 18 reads `SYNTAX      Gauge32`, external:false, bundled:false, diagnostics:[]).
Seeding before mount is not cosmetic: MibEditorPanel measures the character width exactly once, in onMount, from the mirror element (`cw = charWidth(mirror)`), and the mirror only exists inside the `{:else}` branch of `{#if !source}`. Open the file after mount and cw stays at its 7.2 default while the resolved font may be Consolas at 6.6px/char — every squiggle then drifts right by (col-1) x 0.6px, about 10px at column 17. Seeded before mount, the measurement is real and the underlines land exactly under the tokens.

AFTER mount, one macrotask later (setTimeout 0 / rAF):
  c) `mibEditorStore.setBuffer(BROKEN)` where BROKEN is the text above with `Integerr32` on line 18. This marks the buffer dirty (orange "unsaved" chip in the toolbar, unsaved dot on the Ctrl+7 tab, Revert and Save both enabled) and schedules refresh() 350 ms later, which calls MibEditorAnalyse and paints the diagnostics.
  Simpler alternative if you do not want the dirty state: skip (c), put the five diagnostics straight into SOURCE.diagnostics, and call `mibEditorStore.refresh()` once so the fix bar gets its `missing` list. Save is then greyed out and the shot reads as "just opened" rather than "being worked on" — I would take the dirty version.

CAPTURE at ~1200 ms: after the 350 ms debounce and the stub's promise, before nothing (there is no animation to wait out). Between 0 and 350 ms the status pill says "Checking…" instead of "2 error(s)".

WINDOW SIZE: use --window-size=1600,1000 (with --force-device-scale-factor=2). The surface is flex:1 under ~340px of chrome (header, tabs, toolbar) and above ~200px (status + fix bar + problems), so 1000px of viewport gives roughly 36 lines at 18px — enough for BOTH squiggles (lines 18 and 32) plus the row-access one at 43 just off the fold. At 900px you get ~31 lines and the duplicate-OID underline falls below the fold; its row is still the third in the problems list, but the shot is weaker.

=== 4. THE REST OF THE FRAME ===
- Left rail: ~20 files, filter box empty, ACME-POE-MIB row highlighted in accent-blue as the active file, bundled MIBs carrying a dim diamond, IF-MIB carrying an orange plus-minus (bundled, modified) — one small detail that says this installation has been lived in.
- Toolbar: "ACME-POE-MIB" + the "unsaved" chip, greyed undo/redo (there is no history unless a real input event fired — accept it), Insert, Symbols, Revert, Save.
- Status bar: "90 lines" / "LF" / red "2 error(s)" pill.
- Fix bar (accent-tinted): "Used but never imported: ifIndex, TruthValue (2 in total)." with an "Add to IMPORTS" button.
- Problems list: five rows, severity word colour-coded (red/red/orange/orange/grey), position column "4:5, 18:17, 32:11, 43:5, 83:1" in monospace, message, then the code (unused-import, unknown-type, duplicate-oid, row-access, no-description) dimmed on the right. THIS is where the message and the line live — there is no diagnostic tooltip in this editor.
- Tab strip: keep the other tabs' badges alive from the sibling scenes (trap count, unacked events) so the app looks used.

=== 5. OPTIONAL FLOURISHES ===
- HOVER CARD: it resolves the word under the pointer against the SYMBOL CATALOGUE, so it can never appear over `Integerr32` (a typo is in no MIB). To show it, hover a real symbol, e.g. `Counter32` on line 27. Recipe after everything has settled: rect = textarea.getBoundingClientRect(); clientX = rect.left + 8 + ((col-1)+0.5)*cw - textarea.scrollLeft; clientY = rect.top + 8 + ((line-1)+0.5)*18 - textarea.scrollTop; dispatch a bubbling MouseEvent('mousemove') with those coordinates on the textarea and wait 250 ms (the handler debounces at 220 ms). The card renders name / module / OID / first line of description. It is 320px wide and drops 18px below the pointer, so it will cover three lines of code — I would leave it out of the primary shot and use it for a second, cropped image about the symbol catalogue.
- FIND BAR: dispatch KeyboardEvent('keydown',{key:'f',ctrlKey:true,bubbles:true}) on the textarea, then set #mib-find's value through the native input setter and dispatch 'input'. Searching "acmePoe" gives ~30 orange match boxes and "1/30" in the counter. Deterministic but fiddly; the overlay boxes use the same cw arithmetic as the squiggles, so it only looks right with the pre-mount seeding above.
- The Insert / Symbols dropdowns and the completion popup are component-local state with no external handle; do not plan a shot around them.
hazards: MISSING EXPORT = BLANK APP. The stub module frontend/wailsjs/go/main/App.js must export every name the panel and the store import, or the ES import throws 'does not provide an export named X' and nothing renders at all. The twelve this panel needs: MibEditorList, MibEditorOpenExternal, MibEditorSave, MibEditorRestoreBundled, MibEditorReload, MibEditorSymbols, MibEditorFixImports (MibEditorPanel.svelte:15-23) and MibEditorRead, MibEditorAnalyse, MibEditorSaveDraft, MibEditorReadDraft, MibEditorDiscardDraft (stores/mibEditorStore.js:2-8). MibEditorValidate, MibEditorCheckImports and MibEditorListDrafts exist in Go but are unused by the frontend.

NO FILE IS OPEN BY DEFAULT and no localStorage key can open one — mibEditorStore is memory + a Go-side draft file. Without a programmatic openSource()/open() the screenshot is a centred book icon and one sentence of placeholder text.

cw IS MEASURED ONCE, IN onMount, FROM AN ELEMENT THAT ONLY EXISTS WHEN A FILE IS OPEN (MibEditorPanel.svelte:188, mibeditor/metrics.js:24). Open the file after mount and cw stays 7.2 while Chrome on Windows resolves Consolas at 6.6px/char — squiggles, find boxes and the completion anchor all drift right by ~0.6px per column. Seed the store BEFORE the app mounts.

MibEditorRead's Diagnostics are mib.Validate only — syntax, missing END, BOM, tabs, >200-char lines. The semantic diagnostics that make this panel interesting (unknown-type, duplicate-oid, row-access, no-description, unused-import) and the missing-import list exist ONLY in MibEditorAnalyse's return. A stub that only implements MibEditorRead produces an editor with an empty problems list and no fix bar.

The overlay filters `d.line > 0 && d.severity !== 'info'` — an info-severity diagnostic is listed but never underlined, and a diagnostic with line 0 (a positionless syntax error) is invisible in the text. Only the first 200 marks are drawn.

MibEditorSymbols must return BOTH keys. `catalogue = (await MibEditorSymbols()) || {modules:[],symbols:[]}` guards null but not `{}`; catalogue.symbols.find() then throws on the first mousemove over the code and, being inside a Svelte reactive/event path, can take other reactive statements down with it.
A rejected promise from MibEditorList (or MibEditorSymbols swallowing aside) paints a red toast for 5000 ms over the top-right of the shot. Resolve everything; never reject.

Timing: setBuffer debounces the analysis by 350 ms (mibEditorStore.js:121) and the draft write by 1200 ms. Capture before ~400 ms and the status pill reads 'Checking…' with no squiggles. Notifications live 5000 ms (stores/notifications.js), so any toast raised during the scene will still be in a 1.2 s capture.

No wailsjs/runtime events at all in this panel or its store — nothing to fake here. The shell around it does use EventsOn (eventsStore, pollingStore, trapStore, updateStore, DiscoveryPanel) and OnFileDrop/OnFileDropOff (App.svelte:33), plus InitializeNotifications/SendNotification/IsNotificationAvailable from utils/nativeNotify.js; the stub runtime module must export those or the shell fails to import.

The highlighting mirror needs a REAL layout, not just real data: the transparent textarea sits on top of a <pre> and the two must lay out identically. Both are set to `ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, monospace` at 12px/18px, so any headless environment lacking a monospace face still keeps them consistent with each other, but the squiggle arithmetic only agrees with the glyphs if cw was measured (see above). Only the visible window plus 40 lines of margin is coloured (renderWindow, mibeditor/render.js:22): unrendered lines are emitted as blank lines to preserve height, so a screenshot scrolled far down still paints correctly, but anything that inspects the mirror's HTML sees blanks.

The theme default is dark ONLY because App.svelte removes data-theme for dark; with settings.theme='system' headless Chrome reports prefers-color-scheme: light and you get the light palette. Seed theme explicitly.

If settings exists in localStorage, settingsStore calls decryptSettings on load, which imports SettingsSeal/SettingsOpen/SettingsAdoptKey/SettingsKeyStatus/SettingsForgetKey from the bridge (utils/crypto.js:2-8). Those exports must exist even though nothing in this panel uses them.
canvas is used exactly once, by charWidth() via ctx.measureText — headless Chrome supports it, but if it ever returns 0 the code falls back to 7.2.

document.execCommand('insertText') is the only way this editor writes into the textarea (insertAtCaret, replaceRange). It is not on the load path, but any scene that tries to simulate typing must go through it or the buffer and the DOM disagree.

Two scenes, both requiring the settings modal open on its 4th tab. That state is component-local (SettingsModal.svelte:16 `let activeTab = 'general'`, App.svelte:52 `let showSettings = false`) with no store and no URL hook, so the scene script must, after mount: dispatch `new KeyboardEvent('keydown',{ctrlKey:true,key:','})` on window (App.svelte:352 opens the modal), then `document.querySelectorAll('.modal .tabs .tab')[3].click()`. Do not try tabRequest — App.svelte:257 sets showSettings=false on any tabRequest.

SCENE A — "a configured system" (the hero). Viewport 1280x900 or wider (the modal is capped at 650px, content at 70vh; the three sections total ~580px and fit without scrolling at 900px tall). Content, top to bottom: 3 destinations, each with the green "credential set" chip, the email one also carrying the amber "masked" chip — so both chip styles appear; the syslog row reads `tls://collector.corp.example.net:6514`, the webhook row the full Slack URL with `{{secret}}` in it, the email row `smtp-out.corp.example.net → noc@corp.example.net, oncall-network@corp.example.net`. Then 3 rules, priorities 10 / 20 / 100 in the tabular-nums gutter, the middle one carrying the amber "stops" chip and reading `threshold, reachability · ≥ Major · 10.0.0.0/8 → On-call mail relay, NOC syslog (TLS)`, the last reading `all categories · ≥ Warning → Slack #alerts-network`. Then the delivery log with the red "1 given up" chip beside its heading, the "All" filter button active, and 6 rows: four SENT (grey), one PENDING (amber, 2 attempts, red retry line `dial tcp 10.0.0.25:587: i/o timeout`), and one DEAD (red state, red row tint, 6 attempts, a "Try again" button, and the red error line `550 5.7.1 relay access denied for <oncall-network@corp.example.net> (smtp-out.corp.example.net)`). That one dead row is what makes the shot read as an operated system rather than a demo — it is the only visual proof the outbox has a failure path. Everything is empty by default here: with no fixtures the panel is three grey sentences ("No destination yet…", "Add a destination first.", "Nothing has been delivered yet.") and reads as a fresh install.

SCENE B — "the template editor with a live preview". Same setup, then open the Slack sink's pencil (`document.querySelectorAll('.notify-settings .list li')[2].querySelectorAll('.btn-copy-small')[1].click()`), and WAIT at least 300 ms for the debounced preview. Viewport must be ≥1200px wide (NotifySettings.svelte:1013) to get the two-pane dialog: connection/endpoint fields on the left, template + preview on the right. Best template text is the Slack attachment payload in the NotifyListSinks example above — it uses `{{severityUpper}}`, `{{summary}}`, four `{{name|default}}` fallbacks and `{{tsLocal}}`, so the language's whole vocabulary is visible in ten lines of hand-written JSON; against the `threshold` sample event it renders a complete Slack message. Because payloadMode is `template`, the preview header flips to "Payload preview" and shows the green `valid JSON · 611 bytes` chip beside the threshold/trap/reachability selector — that green chip is the single most convincing pixel in this panel, because it proves the app checked the bytes it will actually POST. Set showVariables=true (`document.querySelector('.tpl-head .btn:last-child').click()`) only if you want the 22-chip variable grid; it pushes the preview down, so prefer it as a separate third shot. For a shot that shows a SUBJECT line instead of a payload, open the email sink: kind!=='webhook' means json:false, and the pv-subject renders `[MAJOR] ifInOctets reached 912.5, above 900, on 10.0.0.1` in bold above the plain-text body.
hazards: Static imports are fatal, not degrading. NotifySettings.svelte:9-21 imports eleven names and TemplateEditor.svelte:5-9 imports three; a single missing export makes the module fail to evaluate and takes the entire app down with 'does not provide an export named X'. All fourteen must exist: NotifyListSinks, NotifySaveSink, NotifyDeleteSink, NotifyTestSink, NotifyListRoutes, NotifySaveRoute, NotifyDeleteRoute, NotifyClearSinkSecret, NotifyListDeliveries, NotifyRetryDelivery, SecretsBackend, NotifyTemplateVariables, NotifyPreviewTemplate, NotifyDefaultJsonPayload.

The preview is on a 200 ms debounce (TemplateEditor.svelte:53-62) and `preview` starts null, so the whole <div class="preview-body"> is absent until the first answer lands. A capture taken immediately after opening the sink editor shows an empty bordered box with only the header. Wait ≥300 ms, or use --virtual-time-budget.

TemplateEditor binds `sink.template.subject` and `sink.template.body` with bind:value (lines 147, 157). If a stubbed sink comes back with no `template` key — which real Go DOES for an untouched sink, because SinkConfig.Template is `json:"template,omitzero"` — the list→edit path survives (NotifySettings.svelte:306 spreads a default) but any scene that constructs editingSink directly throws a TypeError and the dialog never paints. Always ship `template: {subject:'',body:''}`.

reload() is a single try/catch over three awaits (NotifySettings.svelte:36-43): if NotifyListSinks rejects, routes and deliveries are never fetched and all three sections show their empty state plus a red toast. A stub that forgets the (state, limit) signature of NotifyListDeliveries, or returns undefined from any of the three, produces a panel that looks like a fresh install rather than an error.

Both list endpoints are `([]T, error)` in Go, so the JS gets a rejected promise on failure — but they also return a non-nil empty slice on the errNoStorage path (app.go:1189). Do not have the stub resolve `null`; the `|| []` guards cover it, but `deliveries.filter` on the reactive deadLetters line (:153) runs before that guard on a re-assignment.

Delivery timestamps are rendered by formatTimestamp(), which hard-codes toLocaleString('fr-FR') — every shot shows DD/MM/YYYY regardless of the app locale. Feed RFC3339 UTC strings ('2026-09-03T14:41:12Z'); anything unparseable renders 'Invalid Date' across the column.

d.sinkId must match a sink id from NotifyListSinks, and route sinkIds likewise: sinkName() (:257) silently falls back to printing the raw UUID, which is exactly what a broken configuration looks like.

$_('events.severity.' + r.match.minSeverity) is called unguarded whenever minSeverity is non-empty (:338). A value outside info|warning|minor|major|critical prints the raw key 'events.severity.foo' in the rule list.
Nothing here needs a canvas, a chart, a real timestamp RANGE, or a network font — icons are inline SVG strings from frontend/src/icons.js via Icon.svelte, so no icon library has to load.

The sink editor is a position:fixed overlay at z-index 1400 and escapes the 650px settings modal, but its two-pane layout is gated on a min-width:1200px media query against the VIEWPORT. At --force-device-scale-factor=2 the CSS viewport is still whatever --window-size implies divided by nothing — set the window ≥1200 CSS px wide or the template editor collapses to one column and the preview drops below the fields.

The scene cannot reach this panel through localStorage alone. showSettings (App.svelte:52) and SettingsModal's activeTab (:16) are plain component variables; the harness must synthesise the Ctrl+, keydown and click the fourth .tab. Worth stating in the scene definition, since every other panel in this project is reachable by state alone.
